# Interndex pipeline

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-agent-playbook.mjs from lib/agent/playbook/phases.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Interndex holds the playbook, David's standards, his saved rules and his story library. Always start by calling `get_playbook` with the phase below: its standards and saved rules override anything here.

## Run: job description to built resume

Phase: `run`. David pastes a job description, or asks to run on a posting.

1. Work through every step without stopping for approval. Ask David nothing mid-run unless a step below says to.
2. If the posting is already in Interndex, call get_application_brief and get_run_state for it and continue from the first step not marked done. Never redo a done step unless David asks (then pass force: true). Never call get_job during a run; the brief has what you need.
3. Read the posting once and extract: company, exact posting title, location, the employer's job id, the posting link, partner functions the role works with, and the requirements (mark each must_have or nice_to_have). Call create_application_from_jd once with all of it. If it reports an existing application, use that id.
4. Fit read. First check only the posting's own stated eligibility (graduation window, degree level, year of study) against the profile in this playbook. If they rule David out, stop and say why in one line. Otherwise decide: verdict (strong fit, stretch, long shot), each requirement matched to a story, true gaps, words to mirror, and the template (zero2sudo for PM, TPM, data, AI and solutions roles; jakes for consulting and business roles).
5. Never mention work authorization, school semesters or terms, IBM, or other applications anywhere in the run.
6. Tailor with the Positioning playbook in the standards below. Call search_stories once with the requirements, the angles the role calls for, and the template. Reuse library variants first. Write a new bullet only where no variant fits, at most 2 drafts per new bullet, and give every new number an explain note David could say in two sentences.
7. Call check_bullets on the whole page with the template. Fix every failure and check again. Warnings are for your judgment; fix the ones that are real. Never show David a page that has failures.
8. Save and build with one complete_run call: the fit read, the resume content, new variants with their explain notes, and any cover letter or answers. Do not wait for approval before building.
9. Finish with one short summary: the fit read, the PDF link, the posting link, and new explain notes next to the bullets that use them. If the posting asks for a cover letter or questions, draft them from the library and search_answers and include them. No explanations unless David asks.
10. If David changes anything while applying, use rebuild_with_edits with his exact edits. Each edit is saved with record_edit. Save any general instruction he gives with add_rule.

## Library session: write and polish story variants

Phase: `library_session`. David asks to work on the story library, add a new story, or fill angle gaps.

1. Load the library with search_stories for the angles or requirements David names.
2. Convert story_voice variants to house style, add new stories David describes, and write consulting, PM and data versions of stories that lack them.
3. Run check_bullets on every new variant and fix every failure before saving.
4. Give every variant an explain note: one line David could say in an interview, drafted from the story's context.
5. Save each variant with save_variant (source library_session). Show David one compact list at the end, not one message per variant.

## Import: seed the library from David's resumes

Phase: `import`. David shares his recent resumes to set up the story library. Run once; running again changes nothing.

1. Read every resume David shares. Group the bullets into stories (about 25 in total): one story per piece of work, with all its wordings as variants.
2. For each experience record the organization, official title, start and end month, and location exactly as the most recent resume states them.
3. Tag each variant house or story_voice using the standards below. Mark the gold set bullets in the standards is_gold.
4. Draft a one-line explain note for every variant that has a number. Show the notes as one compact list per experience; David approves all or fixes lines.
5. Ask David once for the fit-read profile if this playbook shows none: graduation month and year, degree and program, year of study.
6. Call import_library with the experiences, stories, variants and profile. It is safe to call again: anything already saved is skipped.
